text:
ana: quick idea dump — hedging decisions should be capacity-aware to avoid oscillation when tenants have mixed dedicated+burst quotas. current router hedges cause ping-pong.

 tom: +1, saw this during yesterday's load test. hedged requests hit shared pool, then trigger preempts that move work back. nasty.

 rene: are we thinking of moving this into policy-layer or keep it router-local? both have tradeoffs.

 ana: prefer a small admission contract at router boundary + a stateless policy call that maps (pool_snapshot, tenant_profile, cost_tier) -> allowed_parallelism. router enforces admission checks first.

 tom: what does pool_snapshot look like? granular tokens? occupancy percentage?

 ana: proposal: pool_snapshot = {pool_id, region, headroom_pct, seq, recorded_at_ms}. headroom_pct is coarse (0-100) to reduce churn. we also emit a staleness flag if recorded_at_ms > now-600ms.

 rene: coarse pct keeps bandwidth low. but policy simulation wants determinism. how do we reconcile live signals with offline sim?

 policy-bot: reminder: policy decisions used in canaries must be reproducible from recorded inputs. any runtime-only non-determinism must be captured in the sim artifacts.

 ana: plan: 1) routers will log pool_snapshot along with request traces. 2) sim harness ingests recorded snapshots and replays them deterministically. 3) policy DSL primitives will be pure functions of the snapshot + tenant metadata.

 tom: DSL primitives — we need lease_state(tenant) and snapshot_band(snapshot) maybe. sketch: `lease_state(tenant) -> {DEDICATED, SHARED_BURST, NONE}` and `headroom_band(headroom_pct) -> {FULL, OK, LOW, EMPTY}`.

 rene: also need a way to declare resilience to stale snapshots in DSL. e.g., `if snapshot.stale then conservative_band`. could be implicit.

 ana: yes. runtime rule: if stale -> treat as LOW unless tenant is DEDICATED. keep dedicated safe.

 sam: metrics to capture: hedge_invocations, hedge_parallelism, hedged_to_shared_count, preemptions_after_hedge, trace_pool_seq. add histograms for decision latency.

 devops-bot: note: routers already heartbeat capacity every 1s. reducing to 500ms increases network chatter. suggest we keep 1s but include delta since last heartbeat for burst detection.

 tom: good point. delta can help detect sudden frees. maybe policy can prefer increasing parallelism only when delta>threshold. prevents optimistic hedging.

 rene: edge case: cross-region tenants. we should default to region-local headroom. enable cross-region hedging only via tenant opt-in. policy DSL: `allow_cross_region(tenant)` knob.

 ana: rollout path: A) implement a read-only policy endpoint that takes snapshot and returns `band` (no enforcement) — run in shadow for 2 weeks. B) add admission split (MUST_USE, REJECT, PROVISIONAL) behind FF. C) enable enforcement gradually. D) expose runtime flags for emergency constraints.

 sam: simulation requirements: generate synthetic snapshot timelines with intermittent staleness, lease transitions, and network jitter. assert: preemptions_after_hedge decreases by >25% and 99p latency not worse than baseline.

 policy-bot: also add a regression test that replays a recorded incident trace and checks the new policy wouldn't have increased customer-visible errors.

 tom: implementation notes: keep policy endpoint idempotent and side-effect free. do not allow it to trigger reconfig. routers must still make final admission decisions locally when policy is unreachable. fallback = conservative (no hedge).

 rene: config; keep band->parallelism mapping in policy repo (versioned). runtime flags (emergency_max_parallel, force_no_cross_region) live in runtime config and are read-only during sim. make sure sim binds a specific runtime flag snapshot.

 ana: small API sketch: `POST /policy/hedge_decide {tenant_id, pool_snapshot, cost_tier, request_meta} => {advice: BAND, max_parallel:int, reason:"...", pool_seq:"1234"}`. include pool_seq for traceability.

 sam: op notes: add audit log when `advice.max_parallel` > current default so we can review changes pre-rollout.

 devops-bot: caution: rolling out more policy calls increases p90 request path latency. make calls async where possible; allow routers to cache advice for 200ms per pool+tenant combination.

 tom: caching ok, but must attach advice_seq to traces. if cached advice used, mark as cache_hit.

 rene: final thought: ensure backwards compatibility for older routers by having the policy endpoint accept missing `pool_snapshot` and respond with `advice: CONSERVATIVE`. log metric for compatibility fallbacks.

 ana: ok i'll draft RFC with the API contract, DSL primitives, sim harness plan, and rollout checklist. assigning followups: @rene will propose DSL signatures, @sam will design sim scenarios, @tom will prototype router shim.

 rene: on it.

 sam: starting sim matrix today.

 tom: prototype tomorrow.
